requirements.note: Arch runs on any x86_64 machine with 512 MiB RAM, and a basic install takes less than 2 GiB of disk. The live installer itself needs more memory, and packages are fetched from a mirror during installation.

page.description: Arch Linux editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A rolling, do-it-yourself distribution: one monthly install image, a package manager that stays current, and no desktop unless you install one. There is one architecture, x86_64.
pros: Rolling release: the monthly image installs a current system, and pacman keeps it current.
Minimal by design: nothing is installed that you did not choose.
The same image is an installer and a rescue system.
The ArchWiki documents almost every step and piece of hardware.
cons: The official guide is a manual, command-line install, including partitioning.
No desktop, browser or office suite on the ISO: you add everything after boot.
No support branches and no end date; you are the maintainer of your system.
x86_64 only. Arch Linux ARM and other ports are separate projects.

editions.name: Installer
editions.description: The only official installation image: a live x86_64 system with the installer, archinstall and the rescue tools, built monthly from the current repositories.
editions.usbNote: x86_64 only. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick. The installer then partitions and formats the target disk.
